newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 slips slightly, blue chips stagnate.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 slips slightly, blue chips stagnate.

text.p: The Czech PX50 edged slightly lower at Monday's close despite a late rally from the index's most heavily capitalised share SPT Telecom.
The PX50 fell 0.2 percent to 556.6 while the major issue dominated RPIX rose 0.04 percent to 1,161.4.
Blue chips continued to chart an uncertain course but dealers said they were hopeful of a boost from a predicted spate of new foreign buying.
"More foreign capital is awaited. No-one wants to sell at lower prices. Everyone belives that the foreign capital will come," said Tomas Michalek of Raiffeisen Capital & Investment.
"The start of the next month will decide it," he added.
SPT Telecom closed 30 crowns to 3,400 and CEZ gained two crowns to 1,070. Komercni Banka lost five crowns to 2,370 and ceska Sporitelna dropped five crowns to 315.
In the broader market Pivovar Radegast rose 222 crowns to 4,663, PVT fell 180 crowns to 3,520 and BVV Brno dropped 171 crowns to 3,251.
The Prague Stock Exchange also announced on Monday that it would delist around 400 mainly low-liquidity shares by the end of June, starting with an initial 100 by the end of March.
